problem: The point $H$ has spherical polar coordinates $(\sqrt{3},\frac{4\pi }{3},\frac{5\pi }{6}).$ Find the Cartesian coordinates of $H.$
worked_solution:
If $(\rho ,\theta ,ϕ)$ are the spherical coordinates of a point, then its Cartesian coordinates $(x,y,z)$ can be found by using the following formulas:

$$
x=\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,y=\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,z=\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ
$$

Calculating $x$, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ \\  & =\sqrt{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{4\pi }{3})\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{5\pi }{6}) \\  & =\sqrt{3}\cdot (-\frac{1}{2})\cdot \frac{1}{2} \\  & =-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

Calculating $y$, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ \\  & =\sqrt{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{4\pi }{3})\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{5\pi }{6}) \\  & =\sqrt{3}\cdot (-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2})\cdot \frac{1}{2} \\  & =-\frac{3}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

Calculating $z$, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}z & =\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ \\  & =\sqrt{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{5\pi }{6}) \\  & =\sqrt{3}\cdot (-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}) \\  & =-\frac{3}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the Cartesian coordinates of $H$ are $(-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{4},-\frac{3}{4},-\frac{3}{2}).$
